summary: Preaching from Galatians 1:6-10, Steve looks at Paul's sharp rebuke of the Galatian church for drifting toward a distorted gospel. He builds three points from it: the best way to know and hold onto the true gospel is to spend real, prayerful time in God's Word; false teaching is common and shows up in many forms, from the legalism Paul confronted to today's "TikTok theologians"; and sometimes we deceive ourselves, whether by avoiding the parts of Scripture that convict us or by quietly adding our own requirements onto a gospel that only ever asked for repentance and faith. He closes with a call to boldness -- there is only one gospel, and Christians shouldn't be ashamed to say so.
takeaways: The best way to know and understand God's Word is to spend real, prayerful time in it -not just consume it passively. False teaching is common and comes in many forms, old and new. Test everything against Scripture itself, no matter how credible or confident the source sounds.
We can deceive ourselves too -- avoiding conviction, or quietly adding our own steps to a gospel that only requires repentance and faith.
